closenessHoursAtHalf.citation: Hours of time together at which closeness reaches half of full closeness; closeness is hours / (hours + this value), so it grows toward full closeness and never reaches it.

spread.citation: Hall (2019), How many hours does it take to make a friend?, Journal of Social and Personal Relationships 36(4): 80 to 100 hours to become a friend, combined across both studies; roughly 50 hours to a casual friend and more than 200 to a close friend.

closenessKinHalfLifeDays.citation: Half-life of time together between relatives without contact, 36 months, as the P15 package and the P13 director use it. Roberts and Dunbar (2015) report kin closeness holding steady while friends' fell, but give no half-life. Calibration check: Mollenhorst, Volker and Flap (2014), Social Networks 37, 65-80 (Dutch panel, 1,007 adults aged 18-65, 604 re-interviewed seven years later): 48% of the discussion partners and practical helpers named at the start were still in the network seven years later, and 30% held the same position (figures as reported in the Utrecht University release of May 27, 2009, ScienceDaily 090527111907; the 2014 article is paywalled and no kin/non-kin split was found in the sources read). The game's share of ties still above their opening closeness after seven years is compared with it in a seven-year run.

spread.reason: No study reports a half-life for closeness without contact; Roberts and Dunbar (2015) report direction only (kin b = 0.27, friends b = -0.62 over 18 months).

closenessOtherHalfLifeDays.citation: Half-life of time together between people who are not relatives without contact, 18 months, as the P15 package and the P13 director use it. Calibration check: Mollenhorst, Volker and Flap (2014), Social Networks 37, 65-80 (Dutch panel, 1,007 adults aged 18-65, 604 re-interviewed seven years later): 48% of the discussion partners and practical helpers named at the start were still in the network seven years later, and 30% held the same position (figures as reported in the Utrecht University release of May 27, 2009, ScienceDaily 090527111907; the 2014 article is paywalled and no kin/non-kin split was found in the sources read). The game's share of ties still above their opening closeness after seven years is compared with it in a seven-year run.

spread.reason: No study reports a half-life for closeness without contact; Roberts and Dunbar (2015) report that friendships decline faster than kinship.

tieMissingWeightPerHour.citation: Pull toward contacting a person for each hour of time together the tie has lost since the last contact. Chosen in a sweep of a 600-resident generated Stanwood, Washington town (56 days, seed p15-opening-kin), where higher values added little contact and crowded out other acts. Checked in a 10,001-resident Sacramento town over 91 days (seed p10-drives-proof-2026-10-09): adults made 47.4 visits a year to relatives outside their home, about 91 hours against 170 in ATUS 2019 (28 minutes a day, Kannan and Veazie 2022), and visited each parent 2.5 times as often as each sibling against 1.37 in the GSS. One discretionary act per activation caps the total.

spread.reason: No source measures how strongly a fading tie pulls a person to make contact.

kinMoveAwayShare.citation: Share of moves out of the county (ACS 2024 B07401, by state and age) that take a person away from their family, rather than to a nearby county or back home. One value cannot reach both PSID 2013 figures (74.8% nearest parent or grown child within 30 miles, 35.5% all of them). In a generated Sacramento town of 3,000 (seed p10-drives-proof-2026-10-09, with later-life re-aging), 0.3 gives 71.1% and 42.4%, and 0.35 gives 67.1% and 37.5%; 0.35 has the smaller combined miss.

spread.reason: No source splits moves out of the county into moves away from family and short or return moves; PSID reports only the resulting distances (74.8% have the nearest parent or grown child within 30 miles, 35.5% all of them).

A survey of 3,000 full-time US workers (Olivet Nazarene University, 2019) found five friends at work on average, a lower bound on coworkers known by name.

spread.reason: No US source on the number of coworkers known by name was found; friends at work (about five on average) bound it from below.

griefResilientShare.citation: Bonanno, Wortman, Lehman et al. (2002), Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 83(5):1150-1164, Results: of 205 widowed adults followed at 6 and 18 months, 94 (45.9%) showed the resilient pattern.
griefResilientShare.estimatedFrom: Taken as the share whose grief has fallen to little by 6 months after a death. The study measured widowed adults aged about 72; the game applies it to every relative's loss (owner ruling, October 10, 2026).

griefChronicShare.citation: Bonanno, Wortman, Lehman et al. (2002), Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 83(5):1150-1164, Results: of 205 widowed adults followed at 6 and 18 months, 32 (15.6%) showed chronic grief.
griefChronicShare.estimatedFrom: Taken as the share whose grief is still above little at 18 months. The 7.8% with chronic depression began depressed before the loss and are not counted here.

griefEarlyCheckMonths.citation: Bonanno, Wortman, Lehman et al. (2002), Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 83(5):1150-1164, Results: of 205 widowed adults followed at 6 and 18 months: the first follow-up, 6 months after the loss.

griefLateCheckMonths.citation: Bonanno, Wortman, Lehman et al. (2002), Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 83(5):1150-1164, Results: of 205 widowed adults followed at 6 and 18 months: the second follow-up, 18 months after the loss.

griefLittleFraction.citation: Share of the grief at a death that counts as little grief when the resilience spread is solved from Bonanno et al. (2002); the study classified people by depression and grief scores, not by a share of starting grief, so this is a modeling choice.

spread.reason: No empirical range identified; Bonanno et al. (2002) classify grief patterns by scores, not by this quantity.

griefPullWeight.citation: Pull of grief toward rest and contact with family, per unit of grief; no direct source.

spread.reason: No empirical range identified; Bonanno et al. (2002) classify grief patterns by scores, not by this quantity.

griefHoldWeight.citation: Hold of grief on organizing, per unit of grief (negative: grief makes organizing less attractive); no direct source. CTO REVIEW 11: grief first pulls toward withdrawal and family.

spread.reason: No empirical range identified; Bonanno et al. (2002) classify grief patterns by scores, not by this quantity.

schoolFinalGrade.citation: U.S. public schools end with grade 12 (the existing game school-calendar.ts: grades 9-12 in high school).

fallingOutBaseRatePerYear.citation: YouGov, February 24-27, 2023, 31,380 U.S. adults: 68% have decided to end a friendship and followed through; https://yougov.com/en-us/articles/45676-americans-ended-friendship-breakups-poll

Each generated peer stands for the missing members of a full class or workgroup, so circles sampled from big places count fully. YouGov counts any friendship over a lifetime, not only classmates and coworkers.

fallingOutConflictWeight.citation: Rise in the yearly falling-out rate per level of each person's conflict trait (log scale); no direct source.

spread.reason: No empirical range identified for how temperament changes the rate of falling out.

fallingOutReliabilityWeight.citation: Fall in the yearly falling-out rate per level of each person's reliability (log scale); no direct source.

spread.reason: No empirical range identified for how temperament changes the rate of falling out.

householdChildAgeYears.citation: BLS American Time Use Survey: household children are those under 18 (ATUS glossary, 'household children'); https://www.bls.gov/tus/glossary.htm

unmodeledLeisureValuePerHour.citation: Score an hour of the leisure the game does not model is worth; an act added to a free block after the activation's pick must score above its hours times this. Calibrated so visits fall on the ATUS 2025 share of people who socialize or communicate on a given day (30.4%, Table 1); no direct source for the value itself. Calibrated on two generated towns of 1,000 residents over 28 days (seeds p15-visit-a and -b: Albertville, Alabama; Kennedale, Texas): 0.4 gave 33.9% and 0.5 gave 28.6% of adult-days with a visit.

spread.reason: Calibrated to one ATUS share; no empirical range for the value of an hour of leisure in these score units.

favorSharedHoursPerYear.citation: Hours of time together a year of sharing a class or workgroup counts for when judging closeness at a later need; Hall (2019) finds about 50 hours make a casual friend and that hours working together count less than socializing; no direct source for a year's worth.

spread.reason: No empirical range for hours of friendship time per shared school or work year.

favorRatePerNeed.citation: Talker Research for Safeway Moving, March 19-25, 2025, 2,000 U.S. adults (opt-in commercial poll): 39% first ask friends for help moving; https://talkerresearch.com/more-than-a-third-secretly-hate-being-asked-to-help-with-moving/

driveCauseHalfLifeDays.citation: Half-life of a drive's pull without new events or acts. spread.reason: No measured persistence of event-born causes exists; the twelve-month grief window is context, not a bound.

volunteerHours.citation: Hours of one volunteering session for a cause group. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: No volunteering-session duration source has been read into the repository yet.

driveConfrontHours.citation: Time spent confronting the person a grudge is held against. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: No measured duration for interpersonal confrontations has been identified.

grudgeRelationshipChange.citation: Relationship level lost on each confrontation. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: No measured bound in this relationship unit has been identified.

confrontImpulse.citation: Stress and mood impulse the confronted person receives. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: No measured bound for this impulse on the core2 affect scale has been identified.

responseCarryOnFit.citation: How strongly a perceived event pushes a person toward carrying on with ordinary life and grieving privately, before their traits lean them; carrying on is the default response. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: The share of bereaved or harmed people who take up a cause is an outcome target for the whole decision, not a bound on this fit.

responseTraitLeanGain.citation: How much a person's trait lean toward a response's act kinds (the shared trait-act table) scales the event's push toward it. Starting value equals the recorded trait scale (traitScale, 3): generated people carry trait values of one on that scale, so the shared table's lean reaches a third of its range, and this gain restores the full range. P10 prototype starting value; calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: No instrument-matched bound links trait-act lean to response choice after life events.

responseAgencyTurnAge.citation: Age at which a person's capacity to form a lasting drive of their own from an event is half of an adult's, rising smoothly (logistic) around it; starting value near the ages when adolescents form durable civic identities and two years below the age of majority. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: Developmental studies describe identity formation across adolescence, not a measured midpoint for event-born drives.

responseAgencyWidthYears.citation: Width in years of the smooth rise in drive-forming capacity around the turn age. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: No measured width for this rise has been identified.

responseCarryOnBaseline.citation: Ordinary life's own pull toward carrying on, independent of the event; a weak event or a person with little agency leaves life as it was. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: The share of bereaved or harmed people who take up a cause is an outcome target for the whole decision, not a bound on this baseline.

driveStrengthScale.citation: How quickly a response's urgency fills a drive toward its ceiling of one: strength rises as one minus the unfilled share times e to the minus urgency times this scale, so drives stay on the same unit as needs. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: No measured bound links event urgency to the strength of a resulting drive.

driveRetireStrength.citation: Strength below which a faded drive stops being rewritten each day; its effect on choices is already negligible and it rejoins if a new event renews the topic. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: A storage floor for speed, not a behavioral quantity; no empirical bound applies.

driveTraceRetention.citation: Most recent decision and act traces the drives module keeps in memory for observers; counts are always exact. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: A memory budget for developer traces, not a behavioral quantity; no empirical bound applies.

responseCauseFit.citation: How strongly a perceived event pushes toward taking up a cause about its topic, before traits lean the person; below the carry-on fit so that only leaning traits form a drive. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: The share of bereaved or harmed people who take up a cause is an outcome target for the whole decision, not a bound on this fit.

responseGrudgeFit.citation: How strongly a perceived event pushes toward holding a grudge against the person responsible, before traits lean the person; below the carry-on fit so that only leaning traits form a drive. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: The share of bereaved or harmed people who take up a cause is an outcome target for the whole decision, not a bound on this fit.

responseGuardFit.citation: How strongly a perceived event pushes toward a resolve to protect one's family, before traits lean the person; below the carry-on fit so that only leaning traits form a drive. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: The share of bereaved or harmed people who take up a cause is an outcome target for the whole decision, not a bound on this fit.

responseAmbitionFit.citation: How strongly a perceived loss pushes toward an ambition to prove oneself (retraining, a new business), before traits lean the person. Calibrated Oct 12 (OPUS-PEOPLE) so that, when every employer in a generated town closes, the share of workers who form this drive matches displaced-worker research: about 10-16% complete retraining (Jacobson, LaLonde and Sullivan 2005) and entrepreneurship rises 2-4 points (Roed and Skogstrom 2014); see data/research/drives/economic-losses.json. Tuned on seeds c1 and c2 (fit 2.0: 17%); checked on fresh seeds c3 and c4: 42 of 329 workers (12.8%).

spread.reason: Fit 1.6 gives 8% and 2.0 gives 17% in the tuning towns; the research band is 10-20%.

responseCallingFit.citation: How strongly a perceived event pushes toward a calling to serve others; lower than a cause because a calling commits a person to lasting service rather than to one condition, before traits lean the person; below the carry-on fit so that only leaning traits form a drive. P10 prototype starting value; no direct source for this coefficient. Calibration against P9 life replays and bereaved/activist cohort spreads is pending and blocks release.

spread.reason: The share of bereaved or harmed people who take up a cause is an outcome target for the whole decision, not a bound on this fit.

resilienceBaseRateScale.citation: Scale at which the SSA 2023 period life table hazard counts against each person's resilience line, with the recorded chronic-condition weights (data/research/health/chronic-condition-pack-2026.json) multiplying it, chosen so expected yearly deaths match the life table applied to the same residents.
resilienceBaseRateScale.estimatedFrom: Calibration probe, October 9, 2026: two generated 10,000-resident towns (Sacramento, California, seed p10-drives-proof-2026-10-09: 0.1064; Kingsville, Texas, seed p10-probe: 0.1052) solved for equal expected deaths over 2021 against the SSA 2023 table. Totals only; no person's outcome is set by it.

resilienceHashDigits.citation: Half of the existing stable hash's sixteen hexadecimal digits (64-bit FNV-1a, src/simulation/ids.ts); two 32-bit halves feed the existing fixed-point survival-line helper (src/simulation/crisis/fixed-point.ts). A generation key, not a behavioral draw.

supplierTradeTermsDays.citation: Net 30 is the most common U.S. business-to-business invoice term; Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta / Small Business Credit Survey and trade-credit literature (e.g., Petersen and Rajan 1997, Review of Financial Studies 10(3)) describe 30-day terms as the norm.
supplierTradeTermsDays.estimatedFrom: Outside supplier bills for a firm's costs are paid one month after the sales that incur them; spread 10 to 60 days across industries.

driveClosureImpulse.citation: Losing one's job when the employer closes: the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Fired at work', 47 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967, Journal of Psychosomatic Research 11(2):213-218), the same anchor the story director uses for a lost job.
driveClosureImpulse.estimatedFrom: Holmes and Rahe (1967) Social Readjustment Rating Scale; spread 0.39 to 0.47 (the scale's 'business readjustment' to 'fired at work')

ownerDistributionBufferMultiple.citation: Firms keep this multiple of their industry's median cash buffer days (JPMorgan Chase Institute, Cash Is King, 2016: openingEmployerCashBufferDays*) before paying owners.
ownerDistributionBufferMultiple.checkedAgainst: Spread 1 to 3; checked against annual closure rate (BDS establishment exit about 8% a year) and town cash staying near its opening level in a calm year.

ownerDistributionLocalShare.citation: Share of a small-town firm's owner payouts received by owners living in the town; ownership of each firm is not modeled yet.
ownerDistributionLocalShare.checkedAgainst: Spread 0.3 to 0.9; the rest goes to owners outside the town.
